source.title: Steering LLMs? Actually, Sparse Autoencoders can outperform simple baselines
source.authors: Mikkel Godsk Jørgensen; Lars Kai Hansen

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figures are not rendered with their plotted values, so numerical results available only in the figures cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether labeled SAE features in language models have causal, target-related effects when steered. This bears indirectly on SAE-recovered features in LLMs, but it does not reproduce or measure toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses superposition as background, but does not test feature overlap, orthogonality, sparsity-dependent geometric transitions, capacity competition, or dimensionality of features. Its own results concern supervised SAE feature selection and feature steering. AxBench ratings and the selected qualitative steering examples are induced by steering; they do not establish how often these behaviors arise without intervention. Figure-only quantitative comparisons are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study uses Gemma Scope SAE features as a steering tool and reports how well its own labelling pipeline performs on AxBench against Wu et al. (2025) baselines and LoRA. It does not measure feature overlap, geometry, capacity competition, polysemanticity causes, whether SAEs recover a model's features, completeness or stability of features, or feature dimensionality. The steering effects are deliberately induced interventions scored as method performance, so none of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that supervised labelling lets Gemma Scope SAE features steer Gemma-2-9b-it close to on par with the LoRA reference, far better than Wu et al. (2025) reported, though still below prompting. They also find that interpretability-selected features are surprisingly causal even without the output score, and that high sparsity (low ℓ0) may not be crucial for steering. Steering did not work well on Llama-3.1-8B with Llama-Scope.
record.recipe_differences: This is not a reproduction of Toy Models of Superposition. It applies SAE feature activation steering and supervised dataset-based feature labeling to language models.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report sensitivity of the labeling pipeline to π0 and the label-support threshold. Steering evaluations vary by layer, forum, SAE sparsity, feature selection, and inclusion of the output score. The study reports that high sparsity does not greatly affect steering performance and that the output score gives a modest improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: Gemma Scope SAE features selected and labelled via supervised Stack Exchange tag probes causally steer Gemma-2-9b-it toward their labels. AxBench aggregated ratings come near LoRA in several fora, and the effect holds even without the causal output-score component. Low versus high ℓ0 matters little. Steering failed on Llama-3.1-8B with Llama-Scope.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correlationally labelled SAE features have causal steering effects matching their labels (SAE feature steerability), independent of high sparsity.

record.problems: The plotted numerical comparisons are unavailable in the supplied text. The authors describe their Danish-student rating trial as small and report no clear evidence of judge bias. Qualitative examples were selected at random but steering strengths were chosen to produce a representative visible effect; some examples fail to incorporate the target concept. Generalization to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct was unsuccessful according to the authors.
record.rows_left_out: No numerical plot values could be recorded because Figures 2, 6, 7, 8, and 9 are not rendered in the supplied text. The appendix reports ordinary-F1 Gemma results, but the prose does not provide a clear outcome suitable for a separate row.

untested.parts: No toy models, geometry, orthogonality, or sparsity transition are examined.
No capacity or importance analysis is done.
No analysis of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of whether features are spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover the model's features. Steering success is reported as method performance only.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested. The paper only notes features are not guaranteed exhaustive.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition and Toy Models are cited only as background motivation for SAEs. Qualitative examples (r7–r17) should not be treated as result rows. Appendix D examples demonstrate LLM-judge mis-scoring, so their concept = 0 values do not indicate absent effects.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature geometry, overlap, orthogonality, or sparsity-dependent transition are measured.
No test of capacity pressure, dedicated dimensions for important features, or feature sharing as a cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Tests causal steering effects of selected SAE features, not feature prevalence across LLMs or whether SAE dictionaries recover the model's full feature set.

No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable across runs or settings, or canonical units. The paper notes that SAE features are not guaranteed to be exhaustive, but does not test completeness.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional subspaces.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Steer selected SAE features using the proposed supervised labeling pipeline; report AxBench aggregated ratings.

conditions.value: multiple selected Stack Exchange fora; individual fora not specified in the prose

rows.baseline: LoRA reference from Wu et al. (2025)
rows.value: The authors report that feature steering is on par with the LoRA reference in multiple fora; exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence intervals computed using non-parametric bootstrapping; values not stated in the text.
rows.note: This is an outcome of intentionally steering selected features, not a measurement of unsteered feature prevalence. The authors say feature steering remains less competitive than prompting overall.
rows.check: This compares the study's own pipeline with LoRA and Wu et al. baselines on AxBench aggregated rating. It is method performance, not a measure of whether SAEs recover the model's sparse features. Values exist only in Figure 2.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Steer selected SAE features and compare concept incorporation ratings with prompt steering and Neuronpedia labels.

conditions.value: Gemma Scope; details as in Figure 2

rows.baseline: Prompt-steering and Neuronpedia reference; exact values not stated
rows.value: The authors report a mostly closed gap between feature steering and prompt steering relative to the Neuronpedia baseline; exact plotted values are unavailable.
rows.uncertainty: Confidence intervals computed using non-parametric bootstrapping; values not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors use concept_rating because it is the AxBench component that depends on the feature-label.
rows.check: Concept-rating comparison of pipeline labels against prompt steering and Neuronpedia labels. This is own-method versus baseline performance. Values are figure-only (Figure 6).

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Compare steering performance using high-sparsity (low ℓ0) SAEs with the other tested SAE sparsity setting.

conditions.value: high sparsity, i.e. low ℓ0, compared with the other tested setting

rows.baseline: Other tested sparsity setting; exact values not stated
rows.value: The authors report that using high-sparsity SAEs seemingly does not greatly impact steering performance.
rows.note: The paper's conclusion is that both low- and high-sparsity SAEs show indications of steering utility; exact plotted values are unavailable.
rows.check: Ablation of SAE ℓ0 on steering utility. It bears on steering method choice, not on any claim version.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Compare selected feature-label pairs with and without the output-score component of the pipeline.
rows.baseline: Pipeline selection without the output score
rows.value: The authors report a modest performance improvement caused by the output score in both low- and high-sparsity SAEs.
rows.note: Exact plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text.
rows.check: Ablation of a pipeline component (the output score). This is own-method performance.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Compare randomly selected features with pipeline-selected features, using the features' original Neuronpedia labels and omitting the output score from pipeline selection.
rows.baseline: Randomly selected features with their original Neuronpedia labels
rows.value: The authors report better feature-steering performance for features selected by the pipeline, even without using the output score; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The prose does not specify which individual layers or fora this comparison covers.
rows.check: Compares pipeline-selected with randomly selected features, both using Neuronpedia labels. This is a feature-selection comparison, not a test of a version.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate feature steering with Llama-Scope SAEs using calibrated F1 for feature labeling.
rows.value: The authors report that they did not manage to steer the model well using Llama-Scope SAEs; exact plotted values are unavailable.
rows.note: The appendix also reports an experiment on Gemma using ordinary F1, but gives no clear explanation for its performance change; that result does not establish SAE feature recovery.
rows.check: Llama-Scope steering failure is a method-generalisation result. No values or baseline are given in the prose.
